title: Exact injective Cech rows and the direct-image total augmentation
statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be topoi presented by small sites in fixed larger coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings $R_X,R_Y$ and module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $f:(\mathcal X,R_X)\to(\mathcal Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with exact module inverse image. Let $V\to1_{\mathcal X}$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of sets, $V_n=V^{\times(n+1)}$, and $v_n:\mathcal X/V_n\to\mathcal X$ the slice localizations with rings $v_n^*R_X$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. All diagrams are small. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories with localization functor $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and finite-diagonal total complexes with differential $d_{\mathrm{Cech}}+(-1)^n d_I$ in Cech degree $n$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Let $I^\bullet$ be any nonnegative complex of injective $R_X$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Set $B^{n,q}=(fv_n)_*v_n^*I^q$ with alternating restriction differential horizontally and $d_I$ vertically. Let $b:f_*I\to\operatorname{Tot}B$ be the localization-unit augmentation with components into the $(0,q)$ summands. For each object $W$ of the chosen site of $\mathcal Y$, let $A=f^{-1}(h_W^\#)$, where $h_W^\#$ is the sheafification of the representable presheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. In $\mathcal X/A$, put $V_A=V\times A\to A$. The sheaf $I^q|_A$ is injective, and direct-image adjunction identifies $B^{n,q}(W)$ with its sections over $V_A^{\times_A(n+1)}$, compatibly with the faces and augmentation. The section complex
$$0\longrightarrow (f_*I^q)(W)\longrightarrow B^{0,q}(W)\longrightarrow B^{1,q}(W)\longrightarrow\cdots$$
is exact: its degree-zero kernel is exactly the restriction image of $(f_*I^q)(W)$, and its higher Cech cohomology vanishes. This includes arbitrary topos objects $A,V_A$, without a representability assumption on the original site. Thus the augmented rows are exact as complexes of module sheaves, and the specified $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism. In particular $Q(b)$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_Y))$. Under transposition of the two double-complex degrees, multiplication on bidegree $(n,q)$ by $(-1)^{nq}$ is a chain isomorphism between the two signed total conventions and is the identity on the augmentation summands $n=0$.

proof.text: Use the canonical elementModuleExtension adjunction to elementModulePullback. The presheaf extension theorem proves finite-limit preservation of the presheaf left adjoint; compose with module sheafification and use the pullback comparison isomorphism to obtain finite-limit preservation of elementModuleExtension. Adjunction.map_injective then proves that every specified element-site restriction of I.X q is injective.

Construct the section comparison as a composite of Yoneda, sheafification, the geometric adjunction, the free-module adjunction, imageIso, and the localization adjunction. To pass the free module through restriction, restrict its sheafification unit: it stays locally bijective because the element projection is cocontinuous. Maps from its sheafification to a module sheaf are therefore equivalent to maps from the restricted free presheaf. Sections on the element site over B correspond explicitly to maps A times B into the underlying module sheaf, by evaluating at (U,b) on a. Verify the resulting comparison on generators. Naturality in the module and D.restriction give a cosimplicial isomorphism; D.unit gives the specified augmentation formula. Additivity follows from naturality with respect to biproduct projections and their sum.

Use injectivity of I.X q on the original site directly. Its underlying module presheaf is injective by the existing sheaf-to-presheaf injectivity theorem. The cosimplicial section object over A times V_n is isomorphic to the Hom complex on the presheaf Cech nerve of A times V to A: products with A identify the sheaf nerves, and the sheaf forget functor preserves finite limits. Apply the existing injective-presheaf nerve acyclicity theorem to this presheaf arrow. Transport vanishing through the nerve isomorphism and then through the section comparison. Thus no separate element-site nerve comparison or representability hypothesis is needed.

Local surjectivity of V to 1 gives local preimages of each section of A under A times V to A: pair the restricted section of A with a local section of V, using the explicit product-evaluation isomorphism. Thus A times V_0 to A is epimorphic, using the explicit V_0 isomorphism to V. It is an effective epimorphism because set sheaves form a regular epi category. A zero cocycle is exactly a map from A times V_0 to the underlying module sheaf agreeing after the two cofaces. For any pair g,h with the same A-coordinate, construct their comparison map into A times V_1 by the universal property of the wide pullback, putting their V coordinates in the two slots. The cocycle equality gives g b = h b. EffectiveEpi.desc supplies a unique descended map from A, proving kernel equals augmentation image; cancellation of the epi proves injectivity. Transport these assertions through the section comparison.

Use the faithful additive functor from module sheaves to presheaves of abelian groups. Exactness is pointwise in this functor category, and any faithful zero-preserving functor between abelian categories reflects exactness. The sectionwise exactness proves the augmented degree-zero short complex exact and its first arrow monic. Higher vanishing proves exactness at every positive degree by the same reflection argument. Construct the canonical map from the complex concentrated in degree zero with fromSingle0Equiv. The short-complex quasi-isomorphism criterion for zero incoming differentials proves it is a quasi-isomorphism at zero; positive exactness handles the other degrees.

The localization unit commutes with $d_I$, and the first horizontal differential kills it: the two restrictions of a section from $A$ to $A\times V\times V$ both forget the $V$ coordinates and therefore agree. Consequently the components into $(0,q)$ give a chain map $b$, since the vertical sign at horizontal degree zero is $+1$. The double complex is first-quadrant: $n\geq0$ by construction and $I^q=0$ for $q<0$. There are only $k+1$ summands on each nonnegative total diagonal. Apply lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation to $B$, $A^\bullet=f_*I^\bullet$, its just-verified unit chain map and the row quasi-isomorphisms of Step 5 (the lemma calls these the resolution columns $B.\mathrm{flip}.X\,q$). Its component hypothesis is exactly our specified $(0,q)$ augmentation. It yields that this $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism, without applying $f_*$ to an arbitrary exact sequence.

By the definition of the derived localization, $Q$ inverts this quasi-isomorphism, hence $Q(b)$ is an isomorphism. Finally let $T$ multiply the summand $B^{n,q}$ by $(-1)^{nq}$ and transpose indices. The transposed total differential is $d_I+(-1)^q d_{\mathrm{Cech}}$. On horizontal arrows the coefficient of $T d$ is $(-1)^{(n+1)q}=(-1)^{nq+q}$, equal to that of $d'T$; on vertical arrows it is $(-1)^n(-1)^{n(q+1)}=(-1)^{nq}$, also equal to that of $d'T$. Thus $T$ is a chain map. Applying it twice gives the identity since $(-1)^{2nq}=1$, so it is a chain isomorphism. At $n=0$ its multiplier is $1$, proving compatibility with the specified augmentation.
